blocks.x: One of the best sports dramas of this decade, Swagger shines a light on the world of youth basketball, including not just the players but their families and coaches. It's high pressure and high stakes. Kids have big dreams and sometimes, so do their parents. And it's not uncommon to come across an obsession with success, which leads to corrupt, unfair practices.

Earning high praise for its two seasons, Swagger is not your typical sports story. It takes you deep into the characters and their relationships and tackles complex social themes. O'Shea Jackson Jr. has been singled out for his especially strong lead performance as Ike "Icon" Edwards. What's especially interesting to know about Swagger is that the story is loosely based on NBA player Kevin Durant's real experiences. Durant himself serves as an executive producer. The show is an essential watch for basketball fans.

blocks.c: Emily Dickinson (Hailee Steinfeld) in 'Dickinson'

blocks.x: One of Apple TV's first shows, Dickinson is a fun interpretation of the life of famous poet Emily Dickinson. Hailee Steinfeld plays a version of the young woman during a time when she's coming-of-age and exploring her identity and finding a way to express herself through prose. As a comedy drama, however, Dickinson is also as wickedly funny as it is a non-traditional period piece.

What's most interesting is that while Dickinson is supposed to take place in the early 19th century, the show weaves in modern language and music, too, so it will appeal to younger fans, even those who aren't familiar with the historical woman. The series also makes mention of historical figures and events. Plus, the show has Wiz Khalifa portraying the character known as Death. You'll also notice some huge names among the recurring and guest stars, including Ayo Edebiri, John Mulaney, and Nick Kroll.

blocks.c: The sisters in Bad Sisters crying

blocks.x: Sharon Horgan created magic with Bad Sisters, an Irish black comedy about sisters coming together in a way they never thought they would. Second-eldest sister Grace (Anne-Marie Duff) is married to John Paul "JP" Williams (Claes Bang), who is clearly not only a horrible husband but also a downright awful man. Grace seems completely lost and under his spell. However, the sisters are unable to get through to her and convince her to leave him. So, they band together to do the unthinkable: kill JP. But they're not exactly stone-cold killers and have no idea how to go about doing it.

The series, one of the best Apple TV shows with five seasons or fewer, follows the ladies' exploits as they try and fail repeatedly to take down this horrid man. The beginning reveals (spoiler alert) that JP is, in fact, dead in present day. The question is, did they actually succeed? If so, who did it and how? Or did JP die some other way? Season 2 follows the ladies as they deal with the fallout from the events in Season 1, and it wraps the story up nicely in a way you wouldn't expect, but that makes perfect sense. Bad Sisters is fun, exciting, and humorous, the chemistry among the cast fantastic.

'Swagger' (2021–2023)

Image via Apple TV

One of the best sports dramas of this decade, Swagger shines a light on the world of youth basketball, including not just the players but their families and coaches. It's high pressure and high stakes. Kids have big dreams and sometimes, so do their parents. And it's not uncommon to come across an obsession with success, which leads to corrupt, unfair practices.

Earning high praise for its two seasons, Swagger is not your typical sports story. It takes you deep into the characters and their relationships and tackles complex social themes. O'Shea Jackson Jr. has been singled out for his especially strong lead performance as Ike "Icon" Edwards. What's especially interesting to know about Swagger is that the story is loosely based on NBA player Kevin Durant's real experiences. Durant himself serves as an executive producer. The show is an essential watch for basketball fans.

'Dickinson' (2019–2021)

Image via Apple TV

One of Apple TV's first shows, Dickinson is a fun interpretation of the life of famous poet Emily Dickinson. Hailee Steinfeld plays a version of the young woman during a time when she's coming-of-age and exploring her identity and finding a way to express herself through prose. As a comedy drama, however, Dickinson is also as wickedly funny as it is a non-traditional period piece.

What's most interesting is that while Dickinson is supposed to take place in the early 19th century, the show weaves in modern language and music, too, so it will appeal to younger fans, even those who aren't familiar with the historical woman. The series also makes mention of historical figures and events. Plus, the show has Wiz Khalifa portraying the character known as Death. You'll also notice some huge names among the recurring and guest stars, including Ayo Edebiri, John Mulaney, and Nick Kroll.

'Bad Sisters' (2022–2024)

Image via Apple TV

Sharon Horgan created magic with Bad Sisters, an Irish black comedy about sisters coming together in a way they never thought they would. Second-eldest sister Grace (Anne-Marie Duff) is married to John Paul "JP" Williams (Claes Bang), who is clearly not only a horrible husband but also a downright awful man. Grace seems completely lost and under his spell. However, the sisters are unable to get through to her and convince her to leave him. So, they band together to do the unthinkable: kill JP. But they're not exactly stone-cold killers and have no idea how to go about doing it.

The series, one of the best Apple TV shows with five seasons or fewer, follows the ladies' exploits as they try and fail repeatedly to take down this horrid man. The beginning reveals (spoiler alert) that JP is, in fact, dead in present day. The question is, did they actually succeed? If so, who did it and how? Or did JP die some other way? Season 2 follows the ladies as they deal with the fallout from the events in Season 1, and it wraps the story up nicely in a way you wouldn't expect, but that makes perfect sense. Bad Sisters is fun, exciting, and humorous, the chemistry among the cast fantastic.
